note: Light Reading (2002-06-24): $3.1M in seed money from the founders and Bessemer, a month after the company opened in Wallingford, Connecticut. On 2003-04-15 it announced over $20M from Bessemer, Highland, Columbia Capital and Silicon Valley Bank, a later priced round well over twice the seed, which graduates the row. Carrier Access bought its product assets for about $8M and hired 30 of its staff on 2007-03-05 (Carrier Access's 8-K), so acquired.

Billing software company. Ericsson announced the purchase on 2014-07-29 and reported it among the acquisitions made in the third quarter of 2014 (its 6-K). Waltham is the address on the company's own Form D of 2012; Ericsson's announcement says Boston. Entry year is the firm's own (1998); no round named.

Reconfigurable signal processing chips for 3G handsets (Campbell, California). Infineon agreed in March 2003 to buy its assets and completed the purchase of the net assets in April 2003 (Infineon's 6-K), so acquired. Entry date is the first year the firm listed it (2002), an upper bound and not an investment year; no round named.

Light Reading (2001-12-03): a $16M first round from Bessemer, Morgenthaler and NEA. A co-investor's SEC filings carry the same purchase as Series A-1 preferred bought in October 2001 and name Bessemer beside it, so the round is read as the Series A. API Nanotronics bought the company's assets in July 2007 (its proxy statement), so acquired; Somerset, New Jersey.

funding_rounds.lead: Bessemer Venture Partners; Morgenthaler Ventures; New Enterprise Associates

note: The firm's own text says NewView Technologies is the former e-STEEL Corporation, so this row and e-steel are one company (New York, from memory). A general counsel's biography shows it still privately held in February 2003; no source read says what became of it. Entry year is the firm's own on the e-Steel listing (1998); no round named.

Freight capacity exchange (NTE, formerly The National Transportation Exchange), Downers Grove, Illinois per its Form D of May 2002. An officer's biography shows it operating into 2002; no source read says what became of it. Entry year is the firm's own (1997); the only financing on record is another investor's purchase of October 1999, so no round named.

Endeca was founded in 1999 as Optigrab (Wikipedia), so this row and endeca are one company, and the answers follow that row: acquired by Oracle in 2011, Cambridge, Massachusetts. Entry year is the firm's own (2000; the endeca row carries the firm's date 2000-02-24); no round named.

Developer of the HDCD audio process (Berkeley, California); Microsoft acquired the company and its intellectual property in 2000 (Wikipedia, and the firm's own listing). The firm first listed it in 2004 as a past exit, so the listing year says nothing about the entry and no entry date is written; no round named.

Procurement software company founded by Marc Porat in 1998 (Palo Alto address on its Form D filings to 2006). It took over Commerce One in 2006 and was itself acquired by Proactis in July 2017 for $132.5M (Wikipedia, Commerce One). Entry year is the firm's own (2000); no round named.

Consumer product advice site (San Francisco). ABC News (2000-12-04) reports that it shut down in October 2000 after its funding was cut off, with about 60 staff laid off. Entry year is the firm's own (2000); no round named.

Supply chain execution software (San Francisco, per Qiva Holdings' Form D filings of 2002). A former director's biography in a 10-K lists it as acquired by TradeBeam; the date was not found. Entry year is the firm's own (2000); no round named.

Continuous data protection company founded in 2001 (Lexington, Massachusetts); Symantec bought it on 2006-12-07 for $20M (Wikipedia). Entry date is the first year the firm listed it (2003); no round named.

Baseband processor designer (fka NetDSP; White Plains, New York). EE Times (2010-11-03) carries an analyst's account that Qualcomm bought it for about $55M, mainly for its patents and without an announcement, so acquired. Bessemer was an existing investor at the $22.5M second round of June 2003 ($14M raised before it), but no source calls the first round a Series A. Entry date is the first year the firm listed it (2002), an upper bound and not an investment year; no round named.

Security management software (fka HyperNOC), Vienna, Virginia per its Form D filings, the last in September 2005. No source read says what became of it. Entry year is the firm's own (2000); no round named.

Maker of flat-plate concentrator solar modules, Santa Clara (its Form D of June 2007). The firm listed it only in 2007 and no source read says what became of it. Entry date is the year of that listing and filing (2007); no round named.

Fabless interconnect chip maker (Marlborough, Massachusetts); Dolphin Interconnect Solutions acquired it in early 2007, its holders taking about 22% of the combined company (Wikipedia). Light Reading (2003-06-16) lists a $6M seed (July 1999), a $20M Series B (July 2000) and a $15M third round whose investor list omits Bessemer; no source says which round the firm entered. Entry date is the first year the firm listed it (2002), an upper bound and not an investment year; no round named.

Lightwave (2001-02-14): founded in March 2000 in Wilmington, Massachusetts, with about $18M of Series A financing from Atlas Venture, Bessemer and Blue Chip; the round is undated between the founding and the article and is read as 2000. Its chief executive left in 2003, the year DuPont set up DuPont Photonics Technologies in the same town, but no page read states a purchase, so the status is unknown.

Web site publishing software company founded by Dan Bricklin in 1995 (Concord, Massachusetts, from memory); Interland bought it in 2003 (Wikipedia, Dan Bricklin). Entry date is the first year the firm listed it (2002), an upper bound and not an investment year; no round named.

EDGAR carries Vibrant Solutions as the renamed Information View Solutions Corp, so this row and informationview-solutions are one company (Fairfax, Virginia). The Rochester Business Journal (2001-05-11) names Columbia Capital and Bessemer as its backers, with $15M raised in summer 2000; TEOCO acquired it in 2006 (an industry profile of TEOCO). Entry year is the firm's own on the InformationView listing (1995); no round named.

basis: Sale consideration (Erik 2026-09-22, decisions.md R6): the firm's own listing says Voyant acquired BVP's portfolio company Octave Communications in 2002 and merged with Polycom the following year. The position in Voyant is what the firm received for Octave Communications, which is its own row (octave-communications); no source read shows a Bessemer round in Voyant before that.

note: E-business services firm. EDGAR carries an Xcelerate Corp in Fort Lauderdale, Florida with a Form D of March 2002, read as this company on the name, the era and memory; no source read ties Bessemer to it, so the city is low confidence. No source read says what became of it. Entry year is the firm's own (2000); no round named.
